 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Don MacAdam was a hockey lifer, and three years out of that life, he devoted himself to the Detroit Red Wings.
 MacAdam, who died earlier this week at the age of 76, was a Red Wings assistant coach on the staff of Jacques Demers from 1986-89. Those were benchmark years for the franchise.
 Oct-1-86:
– Red Wings are paying their coach, Jacques Demers, and their 3 previous coaches: Harry Neale, Brad Park & Nick Polano & Ass't coaches: Colin Campbell, Dan Belisle, Don MacAdam & Dave Dryden
– Tim Raines poised for first batting title

 — 1986 Oilers Day by Day (@OilersDayByDay) October 1, 2026 
 Detroit reached the Stanley Cup conference final in 1986-87 and 1987-88. That was the furthest the team had advanced in the NHL postseason since reaching the 1965-66 Stanley Cup Final.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement When the Red Wings swept the Chicago Blackhawks in the opening round of the 1987 NHL playoffs, it was the first win by the franchise in a best-of-seven playoff series since also beating the Blackhawks in the 1966 semifinals.
 Red Wings Were One Of Many Stops For MacAdam
 MacAdam left the Red Wings organization in 1989. He took over as head coach of the Cape Breton Oilers. They were the AHL farm club of the Edmonton Oilers. Relocating from the Motor City to Maritime Canada was initially a lifestyle adjustment.
 "The first day I pulled into the parking lot at the rink, I had just arrived from Detroit, which was a very different environment to live in," MacAdam told PNI Atlantic News . "I got out of my vehicle and instinctively hit the button to lock the doors.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "One of the guys who worked at the rink was walking by as I locked the door. He turned to me and said, 'You don't have to do that here, b'ye, you're not in Detroit now.'"
 Don MacAdam was an essential part in Hockey Hungary reaching their highest IIHF ranking ever, ranking 16th last year. 
In MacAdam's 4 seasons as the nation's Director of Player Development and President of Hockey Ops, Hungary has more top 16 finishes in the world championships… https://t.co/K2eKQqfi4K 
 — Edward Nicol-McCabe (@Sapsterr_) November 14, 2026 
 MacAdam also coached in the OHL, ECHL, QMJHL, Canadian university hockey, and in Italy and Japan. He is enshrined in the PEI Sports Hall of Fame.
 His final coaching job was with the Hungarian national team in 2023-24. He led the team to the gold medal at the IIHF 1A World Championships, earning promotion to the top division. In recognition of his contribution to Hungarian hockey, MacAdam was honored by the Hungarian Parliament.
